extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, event organizers, communications teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for drafting pre-event and post-event press releases that communicate logistics, news value, and media access. Includes formatting, timing, content elements, and distribution best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise, attention-grabbing; reflects event's main theme/news value; scanned in fraction of a second; include event name and key benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headline short and immediately newsworthy. Make sure it conveys the primary hook or benefit of the event and includes the event name when possible to aid fast scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard format for dateline element in release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE - [City, State] - [Date]" to signal timing and origin of the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening paragraph (5Ws + How)
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph should answer WHO is hosting, WHAT is happening, WHEN (date and time), WHERE (venue, address), WHY it matters, and HOW to attend/register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the essential facts in the lede so journalists can understand and act on the story immediately. Make the registration or attendance instructions clear and prominent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scannable body structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bullet points for key details and short sections to improve scannability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize information into bite-sized blocks (bullets, subheads) so editors and reporters can quickly find facts. Prioritize most newsworthy details early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker and agenda highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: Call out speaker names, titles, session topics, and key agenda items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List notable speakers and what they will address; include short descriptors of credentials or relevance to the news angle to increase media interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable attendees
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify VIPs, celebrities, or industry leaders who will attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlighting prominent attendees strengthens newsworthiness; include affiliations and why their attendance matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor information
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose event sponsors and partners in the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sponsor names, roles, and any relevant sponsorship levels or contributions that affect the event's scope or content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing and registration details
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate ticket prices, registration deadlines, and how to register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a direct registration link or clear instructions; make deadlines and price categories (e.g., early-bird, student) explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press accreditation/process information
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how members of the press can obtain accreditation or press passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contact, deadlines, required credentials, and any on-site press check-in procedures so media can plan coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard hosting organization description that reinforces credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief (one-paragraph) organizational profile with mission, size, and pertinent background; keep it consistent across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-event release timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended send windows for pre-event announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For major events send 4–6 weeks ahead; for smaller events send 2–3 weeks ahead; send a reminder release 1 week before. Always call out registration deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-event release timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: When and what to include in a post-event release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send within 24–48 hours after the event. Highlight outcomes, attendance numbers, quotes from notable speakers, photo/video assets, and plans for future events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended word count and length of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep releases to 400–500 words; one page is ideal to respect journalists' time and improve the chance of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthy angle
rubrics_metrics.description: The release must present a strong newsworthy hook beyond simply announcing an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the event in context — e.g., a debut, record attendance, important policy announcements, or unique speakers — to create editorial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual assets attached
rubrics_metrics.description: Include visuals such as logos, speaker photos, and other multimedia assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-resolution images, captions, and usage rights; offer video assets when available to increase media usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press registration information (best practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear contact and process information for press registration within the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the press contact person, email, phone, and accreditation instructions obvious; note deadlines and any limitations on press access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use embargoes when launching or announcing time-sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly mark embargo times and include embargo contact information; only use embargoes when necessary and be explicit about the terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: All event logistics clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure date, time, venue, and cost are unambiguous in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check venue addresses, time zones, and cost breakdowns; place logistics near the top and in bullet form for quick reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration link/process clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration link or step-by-step process must be obvious and functional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clickable links and fallback instructions (e.g., phone number) and ensure the registration page is live before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker bios and credentials provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide short bios or credential summaries for speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include titles, affiliations, notable achievements, and links to full bios so reporters can quickly vet sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press accreditation process explained
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail the accreditation requirements, deadlines, and documentation needed for press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State if credentials are required, how to request them, contact info for the press office, and any on-site pick-up instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visuals provided (logos, speaker photos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply visual assets to accompany the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to logos and headshots with captions and photographer/credit information; indicate acceptable usage terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: News angle beyond 'we're having an event'
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid releases that only announce an event without a substantive news hook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the event matters to the industry, community, or public and what makes it timely or unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable attendees/speakers featured
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature names and relevance of high-profile attendees or speakers to boost coverage potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context for why these attendees matter and quotes or expected speaking points when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry context provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the event within broader industry trends or issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a sentence or two explaining how the event relates to current developments, data, or policy debates to increase reporters' understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact info for press kit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear contacts for the press kit and media inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List a media contact with phone, email, and availability; include link to a downloadable press kit and indicate what assets are in it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media handles for amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the organization's and event's social media handles for promotion and tagging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suggested hashtags and handles to encourage social amplification and make it easy for journalists and attendees to share.
